A classic art room exercise done with code.

visuals.title: Gravity and planets
visuals.description:
This is a slightly modified version of the example 2.7 in the Shiffman's book "Nature of code."

Note: Surprisingly, the update functions for the movers(planets) implement what is called the symplectic integrator, which preserves exactly the volume of the phase space for the Hamiltonian dynamics. Therefore, the planets on the elliptic orbits never diverge into infinity and never converge into the sun. That is a good characteristics for this kind of simulation.

visuals.title: Particle Text
visuals.description:
Based on https://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/377231.

I was mesmerised by the above sketch, so I decided to experiment with the idea (particle arrival using pixels from an image).

TIP: While experimenting with the idea of the above sketch, I discovered something valuable that could be useful to anyone using the Processing IDE (this does NOT apply to p5 or Processing.js): calling rect(x, y, 1, 1) with no stroke is dramatically faster than ellipse(x, y, 1, 1) and point(x, y). You can test this yourself by pasting this code into the Processing IDE: http://pastebin.com/LU8yXgmD
visuals.instructions: Click to reset the effect

visuals.title: Recursive Tree
visuals.description:
Since everybody got one: Here is my version of a recursive Tree. The text you see at the bottom of the sketch is the seed value for the random generator. Change the seed and see what happens.

Controls:
- TYPE SOMETHING = create seed
- MOUSECLICK = create random seed and generate tree
- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate tree
- ALT = save image

visuals.title: Fluid Simulation + Momentum Transfer + Electrostatic Force
visuals.description:
Mouse-interactive fluid simulation with particles.
The fluid simulation is solved on a 16x16 cell grid.
Using Verlet integration for the particle update.
Every particle has an electric charge and two of them have a static value. When any two  particles collide, they equally share it. The border is the electric ground. There's a nonlinear friction and on every collision there's a tiny amount of 1% energy lost, so its passive state approaches a global lower limit energy.
So far, the binding of the forces is one-way only and the particle motion doesn't add to the fluid simulation.
Have fun!

So far, the binding of the forces is one-way only and the particle motion doesn't add to the fluid simulation.
Have fun!

visuals.title: Blue Mountains
visuals.description:
A mountain range landscape.

Inspired by lesson 38 of Fun Programming: http://funprogramming.org/38-Animate-the-ocean-surface-using-noise.html 

Colors chosen to work on Javascript (the clouds and the sky gradient look different on Java mode). Also, I don't know why, the lerpColor didn't work on Java, it's possible to get the same effect with separated map functions for hue, saturation and brightness though.
visuals.instructions:
Mouse click to generate a new pattern.
Press s to save as an image.

visuals.title: Recursive Tree
visuals.description:
Since everybody got one: Here is my version of a recursive Tree. The text you see at the bottom of the sketch is the seed value for the random generator. Change the seed and see what happens.

Controls:
- TYPE SOMETHING = create seed
- MOUSECLICK = create random seed and generate tree
- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate tree
- ALT = save image

M = direction
N = toggle color
Space = auto rotation

・ 与えられたランダムな点群
・ それを基にした 3次元 Delaunay 分割
・ 内部エッジの除去
・ サーフェスの生成

visuals.title: Kinect 3D scanner
visuals.description:
Simple 3D scanner using the Kinect.

Doesn't work in the browser. You need a Kinect to run it and the controlP5 (version controlP5_1.5.1), hemesh and simple-openni libraries installed. 
 
Select the scanner area with the controls and press the "take scan" button to capture the 3D points inside the box. A mesh is created with the Hemesh library and saved in the sketch directory. The colors of the mesh faces are saved in a different file. Press the "take scan" button again to take more scans. 
 
Use http://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/62533 to read and represent the mesh.

visuals.title: polar.Coordinates
visuals.description:
In mathematics, the polar coordinate system is a two-dimensional coordinate system in which each point on a plane is determined by a distance from a reference point and an angle from a reference direction.
The reference point (analogous to the origin of a Cartesian system) is called the pole, and the ray from the pole in the reference direction is the polar axis. The distance from the pole is called the radial coordinate or radius, and the angle is called the angular coordinate, polar angle, or azimuth.

(Wikipedia)

visuals.title: Fireflies Synchronization
visuals.description:
This is a Processing sketch to simulate the way fireflies synchronize with one another. Each of of the circles represents a single firefly and when another firefly on the screen flashes white, or "fires", the firefly will try and catch up to the firefly that just fired. The world makes many assumptions, so here is a list of some of them:
1) Every firefly can see every other firefly and has 20/20 vision
2) Every firefly starts with the same period
3) Every firefly is influenced additively or linearly by the number of flies firing

visuals.title: Tiny Fibonacci Sphere v2.0
visuals.description:
A fast method of producing an arbitrary number of equally distributed points around a sphere. This is accomplished by drawing a fibonacci spiral (similar to sunflower seed pattern) that maintains constant surface area.

n = number of points
phi = (sqrt(5)+1)/2 - 1
ga = PHI * PI

for each point i (1..n)
longitude = ga*i
latitude = asin(-1 + 2*i/n)

As written, the sketch constantly adds new points to the sphere. Click to toggle this feature, so you can examine the point distribution.

visuals.title: EulerSpirals
visuals.description:
Think like a Turtle: draw straight connected lines of the same length,
that are each deflected (turned in Turtle talk) by an angle. 
This will draw a rough circle. 
If instead, each angle is increased by a fixed amount each step, a spiral flourish is produced.
http://blog.matthen.com/post/67889183164/draw-a-straight-line-and-then-continue-it-for-the

visuals.title: Noise flow Painter
visuals.description:
*It may need a moment to load*

Paints an image with strokes that are rotated by a flow field driven from noise.

If you want to try it on your own image you need to drag and drop an image in the sketch's files tab. Then add your image's file name to the variable imgNames (it's near the top). It doesn't capture details very well so close ups work best.

Controls:
  - Click to change to the next image.
  - Press any key to save the canvas to a jpg.
visuals.instructions: Click for the next image, press a key to save a jpg.

visuals.title: Fireflies Synchronization
visuals.description:
This is a Processing sketch to simulate the way fireflies synchronize with one another. Each of of the circles represents a single firefly and when another firefly on the screen flashes white, or "fires", the firefly will try and catch up to the firefly that just fired. The world makes many assumptions, so here is a list of some of them:
1) Every firefly can see every other firefly and has 20/20 vision
2) Every firefly starts with the same period
3) Every firefly is influenced additively or linearly by the number of flies firing

visuals.title: Tiny Fibonacci Sphere v2.0
visuals.description:
A fast method of producing an arbitrary number of equally distributed points around a sphere. This is accomplished by drawing a fibonacci spiral (similar to sunflower seed pattern) that maintains constant surface area.

n = number of points
phi = (sqrt(5)+1)/2 - 1
ga = PHI * PI

for each point i (1..n)
longitude = ga*i
latitude = asin(-1 + 2*i/n)

As written, the sketch constantly adds new points to the sphere. Click to toggle this feature, so you can examine the point distribution.

- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate tree
- ALT = save image

visuals.title: Dancing Fish
visuals.description:
Tweak of http://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/156580

With this example I focused highly on the calculation of the fish geometry which is realised mostly with vector math and the trigonometric functions. The movement itself has 3 options:
Movement mode 1 = All fish try to reach the mouse
Movement mode 2 = All fish align along a noise field
Movement mode 3 = All fish align along a radial vector field

Controls:
Press mouse or 'space' to change movement mode
Press 'plus' to change the display mode

Video:
https://vimeo.com/113223673

visuals.title: SVG Example
visuals.description: This is an example of copy/paste from Adobe Illustrator, showing how to convert that SVG data into a bezier curve. Note - this is mainly useful if you plan to animate your bezier curves, otherwise just import an image or SVG file directly!

visuals.title: Hover Object Tutorial
visuals.description: This tutorial shows how to code a hover effect by making an ellipse into an object. We go a step further and make a class that we can easily reuse to make multiple hover objects.

visuals.title: Gradient Palette
visuals.description:
A sketch showing how to use a gradient .png file as a palette. To see the gradient, Fork this sketch and download it from the tiles area.

The very last slide uses a lerp function to transition gradually from one color to another. Doing that introduced an interesting Josef Albers conundrum, what are the colors doing in reality versus what our eye perceives?

visuals.title: Mouse Recording
visuals.description: A sketch to record mouse movents into an array.

visuals.title: While Loop

visuals.title: Simple Function

visuals.title: Hover Object
visuals.description: This tutorial shows how to code a hover effect by making an ellipse into an object. We go a step further and make a class that we can easily reuse to make multiple hover objects.

visuals.title: Monster Tutorial
visuals.description: This tutorial shows how to convert Angelica's monster from a bunch of commands in the draw loop, to a function and finally to a class. The advantage of a new object class is obvious on page 5, we can do all sorts of things to it.

visuals.title: Delete Bubble Tutorial
visuals.description: Based on the Click Bubble example, we can also delete a bubble when it is clicked on to delete a bubble from the array. The very last slide converts the Bubbles into a proper class and renames the variables so they are 'self-documenting'.

visuals.title: p5 Play Example
visuals.description: This shows the p5 library installed along with the example sprites.

visuals.title: Ben Day Dot Stub
visuals.description: This sketch loads an image, in preparation of converting it to a halftone pattern (the Ben Day Dot Pattern). It will focus on arrays, looping through an array and getting values to fill each spot on the screen.

visuals.title: JSON Tutorial
visuals.description: This sketch explains how to work with JSON data, including how to properly fetch JSON and deal with errors. The last page of the Tutorial shows a live JSON feed that will fail after a few seconds, and then the backup JSON file will load.

visuals.title: JSON Deserialization Example
visuals.description: This fork of the Intro to JSON Tutorial shows how to deserialize or parse a JSON object into a new class defined in our sketch.

visuals.title: Ben Day Dots
visuals.description: This sketch will take an image and convert it to a halftone pattern (the Ben Day Dot Pattern). It will focus on arrays, looping through an array and getting values to fill each spot on the screen.

visuals.title: Fetching Complex Data Tutorial
visuals.description: This Tutorial shows the p5 examples for fetching data in various ways. The final slide is the method that I needed to use for fetching from an API that requires an Authorization key.

visuals.title: Query an API Tutorial 2

Each particle interacts with every other particle.
When they are too close, they repel.
When they are too far, they attract.
Notice the surface tension!
visuals.instructions: Click, drag or caress the mouse.

visuals.title: Interface
visuals.description:
A 2D model of how oil and water molecules repel each other with different strengths, making them self-assemble into groups. Based on the PhD thesis of Naoaki Ono.

The mouse controls a water molecule so you can push the oil blobs around.

If you want to play it as a game, try this:
Task 1: push all the blobs together into one big blog
Task 2: split the big blob into little blobs. You get more points for the more separate blobs you make.
(Note: there aren't any points, you will have to make up your own scoring system.)
visuals.instructions: Move the mouse to push the oil blobs around

visuals.title: interface 5
visuals.description: Controls: Mouse pressed stops the lines from spiraling inward, and stops showing their paths. Mouse not pressed sends the lines spiraling inward. At first let the mouse hold still in the center for a few seconds, then start. Also try holding down the mouse and moving it around the screen a bit, and then releasing the mouse and hold it perfectly still, watching what happens. The code is relatively easy to figure out, it's a particle system. Enjoy.

visuals.title: Oil-water phase separation
visuals.description:
A 2D model of how oil and water molecules repel each other with different strengths, making them self-assemble into groups. Based on the PhD thesis of Naoaki Ono.

The mouse controls a water molecule so you can push the oil blobs around.

If you want to play it as a game, try this:
Task 1: push all the blobs together into one big blog
Task 2: split the big blob into little blobs. You get more points for the more separate blobs you make.
(Note: there aren't any points, you will have to make up your own scoring system.)
visuals.instructions: Move the mouse to push the oil blobs around

visuals.description:
A simulation of the wheel at the end of a kaleidoscope (before the mirror reflections are added).

This was a proof-of-concept I used before implementing the same code in C++ for an OpenGL kaleidoscope simulation I developed a few years ago.

The physics use Verlet integration, which helps reduce jitter in the motion.

This is based on a Flash program I wrote:

http://www.krazydad.com/bestiary/bestiary_objectcell.html

visuals.title: Triangles Camera
visuals.description:
Detect motion in a live webcam image using pjs, insert particles into a particle system where motion is detected. 
please keep in mind that i'm using hacks to get  pjs to work with the webcam data. your mileage may vary. Code is an unholy marriage between plain JS, HTML5 objects and PJS, so it will not function in the Processing IDE.

this version features several small improvements ; less looping in render method, maximum number of particles, particles follow direction of motion.
visuals.instructions: Open in a browser like Chrome / Safari / Firefox. Turn your webcam on. Wave your hand, turn your head

(unoptimized) Delaunay triangulation with various display modes.

Delaunay triangulation implementation done from scratch. See code for references.

visuals.title: Islamic Stars
visuals.description:
Move the mouse horizontally and vertically to change the image.  X and Y control two different parameters.

This was an experiment with a method used to produce Arabic/Islamic star tiling patterns, from an underlying grid of polygons.

Starting with an underlying grid of polygons, the star pattern is produced by drawing lines from two equidistant points on each polygon edge at some fixed angle (controlled by the mouse).  At the point where the lines would intersect with other lines, they are clipped.

Y controls the distance from the center of the polygon edge.
X controls angle.

visuals.title: EEG-FLOW
visuals.description:
We see the envelope of multiple oscillations from the human resting state EEG during eyes closed. A chunk of 20 sec is plotted clockwise circularly along the outer edge The time series shrinks, changes color and slowly starts to oscillate tangentially as it gets attracted towards the center of the circle, leaving behind multiple traces of itself. A pulsating, hypnotic figure emerges, reminiscent of a sea urchin or a flower

Move mouse towards right-left edge to shrink-grow shape.
move mouse vertically to increase the amplitude of the oscillation of the tangential rotation.
Click to reset

Invert shape: i
Invert colors toggle: b
Random/BW color switch: c

Filter toggle: f
Discrete/Continuous: d

Change number of balls: _,+
Change radius: -,=
Change discretization steps: {,}

visuals.title: Ideal Triangles in the Poincaré disc
visuals.description:
When using the Poincaré disc model for hyperbolic geometry, the hyperbolic universe is inside a circle. The circle itself is at infinity. A triangle inside the circle will always have angle sum < 180 degrees. As the vertices of a triangle approach the circle, the angle sum tends to 0, and the hyperbolic perimeter tends to infinity. The limiting triangle is called an ideal triangle. The hyperbolic area of an ideal triangle is always pi. All triangles in the animation have the same hyperbolic area. 

The animation is used on http://www.malinc.se/math/noneuclidean/mainen.php

visuals.title: Continuity of Bézier splines

Move the points to make the blue curve continuous! (you probably ruin the continuity of the green curve)
Hide the velocity and acceleration vectors and show the mirror points! 
When C2 lies on the grey mirror point C1', the velocity is continuous. 
When the yellow mirror points C0' and C3' coincide, the acceleration is continuous. 
Lock C2 and C3 to an A-shape! Move the other points!

visuals.title: Fluid Simulation + Momentum Transfer + Electrostatic Force
visuals.description:
Mouse-interactive fluid simulation with particles.
The fluid simulation is solved on a 16x16 cell grid.
Using Verlet integration for the particle update.
Every particle has an electric charge and two of them have a static value. When any two  particles collide, they equally share it. The border is the electric ground. There's a nonlinear friction and on every collision there's a tiny amount of 1% energy lost, so its passive state approaches a global lower limit energy.
So far, the binding of the forces is one-way only and the particle motion doesn't add to the fluid simulation.
Have fun!

visuals.title: Ideal Triangles in the Poincaré disc
visuals.description:
When using the Poincaré disc model for hyperbolic geometry, the hyperbolic universe is inside a circle. The circle itself is at infinity. A triangle inside the circle will always have angle sum < 180 degrees. As the vertices of a triangle approach the circle, the angle sum tends to 0, and the hyperbolic perimeter tends to infinity. The limiting triangle is called an ideal triangle. The hyperbolic area of an ideal triangle is always pi. All triangles in the animation have the same hyperbolic area. 

The animation is used on http://www.malinc.se/math/noneuclidean/mainen.php

visuals.title: Poincare Hyperbolic Disk Tiling
visuals.description: This sketch illustrates an algorithm for drawing checkered patterns on the the Poincare disk. The Poincare disk is a model of hyperbolic geometry. The pattern is defined by reflections in the circles shown. For each point we check weather it is inside any of the circles. If not, it must be in that triangular space in the middle,  the only bit thats not inside any of the circles. So we draw that pixel white. Otherwise we repeatedly “reflect” the point until it finds its way to the middle triangle. We then colour it depending on weather it took an even or odd number of reflections.
visuals.instructions: Click on any point to see its orbit to the centre under multiple reflections.

visuals.title: Ideal Triangles in the Poincaré disc
visuals.description:
When using the Poincaré disc model for hyperbolic geometry, the hyperbolic universe is inside a circle. The circle itself is at infinity. A triangle inside the circle will always have angle sum < 180 degrees. As the vertices of a triangle approach the circle, the angle sum tends to 0, and the hyperbolic perimeter tends to infinity. The limiting triangle is called an ideal triangle. The hyperbolic area of an ideal triangle is always pi. All triangles in the animation have the same hyperbolic area. 

The animation is used on http://www.malinc.se/math/noneuclidean/mainen.php

visuals.title: Optical Illusion #5 (Hering Illusion)
visuals.description:
The red lines are straight but appear to be bent.

Explanation by livescience.com:
"Evolution has seen to it that geometric drawings like this elicit in us premonitions of the near future. The converging lines toward a vanishing point (the spokes) are cues that trick our brains into thinking we are moving forward as we would in the real world, where the door frame (a pair of vertical lines) seems to bow out as we move through it and we try to perceive what that world will look like in the next instant."

visuals.description:
Our version of an Italian Word Search using the most common Italian words used in restaurants. Once the user finds a word they can draw a straight line through the letters. Identical to the way a hard copy word search works, they can strike out the found word from the list to the right. There is also a timer function that shows the time passed since the game has started. When the timer gets to 12.59.59 a funny phrase will be printed on the screen.
Every time the game starts a different grid will be printed on the screen.
Click&hold; with left mouse button to draw a line.

visuals.title: Spring force chain
visuals.description:
A series of springs are connected to each other to get a pendulum-like effect.

Inspired by Daniel Shiffman's The Nature of Code (shiffman.net)

Controls:
- Left & right click to add wind force
- Middle mouse click to increase gravity
- Q to increase springs elasticity
- W to decrease springs elasticity
- A to increase mass
- S to decrease mass
visuals.instructions: Check description.

visuals.title: Cloth mesh verlet integration
visuals.description:
Controls:
 - Left & right click to add wind force
 - Middle mouse click to increase gravity
 - Hold 'Q' to cut the cloth
 - Hold 'W' to paint areas to snap points
 - Hold 'E' to paint away areas to unsnap points
 - 'R' to reset the sim
 - 'T' to toggle between building triangulation
 - 'A' to increase timesteps
 - 'S' to decrease timesteps
 - 'Z' to decrease grid's resolution
 - 'X' to increase grid's resolution

visuals.title: Obj viewer
visuals.description:
Reads data from an obj format and displays it.

An obj format is a generic format used by most 3d software packages to describe a mesh. In fact, this model was exported out from Maya.

There's so much more to be done with this, but here's a start!

Controls:
    - Drag left-click to rotate camera.
    - Drag middle-click to move camera.
    - Drag right-click to zoom.
    - E to toggle edges.
    - P to toggle points.
    - F to toggle faces.

*It may need a moment to load*

Paints an image with strokes that are rotated by a flow field driven from noise.

If you want to try it on your own image you need to drag and drop an image in the sketch's files tab. Then add your image's file name to the variable imgNames (it's near the top). It doesn't capture details very well so close ups work best.

Controls:
  - Click to change to the next image.
  - Press any key to save the canvas to a jpg.
visuals.instructions: Click for the next image, press a key to save a jpg.

visuals.title: Fire brush 2 (sprites)
visuals.description:
Another attempt at fire and smoke using sprites.
 
Before I was controlling the image's transparency using 'tint', but this was slowing down the sketch way too much. Instead I'm creating new images in setup but with different transparencies that the sketch can reference to. This removes 'tint' from draw() and boosts the speed of it ten fold.

visuals.title: Facial Rig
visuals.description:
A more extensive test to get a full blend shape facial rig working online.

I had to write a script in Maya to export poses consistently so that verts would blend without jumping around.

Each control captures 4 different states: Up, down, left, and right. When a control is moved, their deltas all applied to a mesh blending between them all to give the final output.

Good times!
visuals.instructions: Drag the points to deform his face
